```{r theme, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Shared look: one palette and one theme for every plot
# ==============================================================================
col_main   <- "#2C7FB8"   # blue
col_accent <- "#D95F0E"   # orange
col_green  <- "#2E8B6E"
col_purple <- "#6A51A3"
col_grey   <- "#6B7280"

theme_proj <- function(base_size = 13) {
  theme_minimal(base_size = base_size) +
    theme(
      plot.title.position   = "plot",
      plot.caption.position = "plot",
      plot.title    = element_text(face = "bold", size = rel(1.25), margin = margin(b = 4)),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(color = col_grey, margin = margin(b = 12)),
      plot.caption  = element_text(color = col_grey, hjust = 0, margin = margin(t = 10)),
      axis.title    = element_text(color = col_grey),
      axis.text     = element_text(color = "grey25"),
      panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.4),
      strip.text    = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0),
      legend.position = "top",
      legend.justification = "left",
      plot.margin   = margin(12, 16, 12, 12)
    )
}
```

```{r table-figure-helper, include=FALSE}
# ==============================================================================
# Save a data frame as a PNG "table figure"
# ==============================================================================
# df            data frame to draw (character columns display best)
# file          output path, e.g. "figures/tbl_example.png"
# title, note   text above and below the table
# align         one of "l", "r", "c" per column (default: first left, rest right)
# wrap          named vector of wrap widths for long text columns,
#               e.g. c(Description = 50)
# bold_last_row make the last row bold (for total rows)
save_table_png <- function(df, file, title = "", note = "", align = NULL,
                           wrap = NULL, bold_last_row = FALSE, dpi = 200) {
  df <- as.data.frame(df, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  nr <- nrow(df); nc <- ncol(df)
  if (is.null(align)) align <- c("l", rep("r", nc - 1))
  if (!is.null(wrap)) {
    for (col in names(wrap)) df[[col]] <- str_wrap(df[[col]], wrap[[col]])
  }

  hj <- unname(c(l = 0,    c = 0.5, r = 1   )[align])
  xx <- unname(c(l = 0.04, c = 0.5, r = 0.96)[align])

  face <- rep("plain", nr * nc)
  if (bold_last_row) face[(seq_len(nc) - 1) * nr + nr] <- "bold"
  fills <- rep(rep_len(c("white", "#F3F4F6"), nr), nc)

  tt <- ttheme_minimal(
    base_size = 11,
    padding = unit(c(5, 3.5), "mm"),
    core = list(
      fg_params = list(hjust = rep(hj, each = nr), x = rep(xx, each = nr),
                       fontface = face, col = "grey15"),
      bg_params = list(fill = fills, col = NA)),
    colhead = list(
      fg_params = list(hjust = hj, x = xx, fontface = "bold", col = "white"),
      bg_params = list(fill = col_main, col = NA))
  )
  g <- tableGrob(df, rows = NULL, theme = tt)

  # Measure the table so the saved image fits it exactly
  pdf(NULL)
  w_tbl <- convertWidth(sum(g$widths), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
  h_tbl <- convertHeight(sum(g$heights), "in", valueOnly = TRUE)
  dev.off()

  title_w <- str_wrap(title, max(25, floor(w_tbl * 8.5)))
  note_w  <- str_wrap(note,  max(30, floor(w_tbl * 12.5)))
  h_title <- if (nzchar(title)) length(strsplit(title_w, "\n")[[1]]) * 0.27 + 0.2 else 0.1
  h_note  <- if (nzchar(note))  length(strsplit(note_w,  "\n")[[1]]) * 0.17 + 0.25 else 0.1

  x_left  <- unit(0.5, "npc") - unit(w_tbl / 2, "in")
  title_g <- textGrob(title_w, x = x_left, y = unit(0.12, "in"), hjust = 0, vjust = 0,
                      gp = gpar(fontface = "bold", fontsize = 14, col = "grey15",
                                lineheight = 1.05))
  note_g  <- textGrob(note_w, x = x_left, y = unit(1, "npc") - unit(0.12, "in"),
                      hjust = 0, vjust = 1,
                      gp = gpar(fontsize = 9, col = col_grey, lineheight = 1.15))

  lay <- arrangeGrob(title_g, g, note_g, ncol = 1,
                     heights = unit.c(unit(h_title, "in"), unit(h_tbl, "in"),
                                      unit(h_note, "in")),
                     widths = unit(w_tbl, "in"))

  png(file, width = w_tbl + 0.6, height = h_title + h_tbl + h_note + 0.4,
      units = "in", res = dpi, bg = "white")
  grid.newpage()
  grid.draw(lay)
  invisible(dev.off())
  invisible(file)
}
```

```{r read-data}
# ==============================================================================
# Reading data
# ==============================================================================
c_df <- read_csv("~/Documents/Davis/DDSC/Analyzing Unemployment Project/cps_monthly_hazards.csv")
p_df <- read_parquet("~/Documents/Davis/DDSC/Analyzing Unemployment Project/cps_master_panel_2005_2026.parquet",
                     col_select = c(RACE, EMPSTAT, WHYUNEMP))

c_df <- c_df |>
  select(U_short, f_shimer, lambda_t)

# RACE is grouped into broad categories from the numeric IPUMS codes. Check the
# groupings against the RACE variable page on IPUMS CPS. Do this BEFORE any
# factor() call on RACE, because it uses the numeric codes.
p_df <- p_df |>
  mutate(
    race_grp = case_when(
      RACE == 100            ~ "White",
      RACE == 200            ~ "Black",
      RACE == 300            ~ "American Indian / Alaska Native",
      RACE %in% c(650, 651)  ~ "Asian",
      RACE == 652            ~ "Pacific Islander",
      RACE == 700            ~ "Other single race",
      RACE >= 801            ~ "Two or more races",
      TRUE                   ~ NA_character_
    ),
    EMPSTAT = factor(EMPSTAT,
                     levels = c(0, 1, 10, 12, 20, 21, 22, 30, 31, 32, 33, 34, 35, 36),
                     labels = c("NIU", "Armed Forces", "At work", "Has job, not at work",
                                "Unemployed", "Unemployed, experienced",
                                "Unemployed, new worker", "NILF", "NILF, housework",
                                "NILF, unable to work", "NILF, school", "NILF, other",
                                "NILF, unpaid work", "NILF, retired")),
    WHYUNEMP = factor(WHYUNEMP,
                      levels = 0:6,
                      labels = c("NIU", "Job loser/layoff", "Other job loser",
                                 "Temp job ended", "Job leaver", "Re-entrant",
                                 "New entrant"))
  )
```

# 1. Data overview

The analysis uses monthly labor market measures (one row per month) and a person-level
panel of survey records (one row per person per month). Both are built from the Current
Population Survey (CPS), obtained through IPUMS.

```{r data-dictionary}
# ==============================================================================
# Data dictionary
# ==============================================================================
data_dict <- tribble(
  ~Variable,    ~`Plain-language name`,              ~Type,            ~Description,
  "U_short",    "Short-term unemployed",             "Monthly count",  "Number of people who have been unemployed for only a short time (under 5 weeks).",
  "f_shimer",   "Job-finding probability",           "Share (0 to 1)", "Chance that an unemployed person finds a job by the next month, corrected for survey measurement error.",
  "lambda_t",   "Job-finding rate",                  "Rate",           "The same job-finding measure expressed as a continuous-time monthly rate.",
  "RACE",       "Race",                              "Category",       "Race group, collapsed from detailed IPUMS codes into broad categories.",
  "EMPSTAT",    "Employment status",                 "Category",       "Whether a person is working, unemployed, or outside the labor force.",
  "WHYUNEMP",   "Reason for unemployment",           "Category",       "Why an unemployed person is out of work. Asked of unemployed people only."
)

dict_note <- sprintf("Monthly measures cover %d months. The person-level panel has %s person-month records. Source: IPUMS CPS, 2005 onward.",
                     nrow(c_df), comma(nrow(p_df)))

# Save the table as a figure
save_table_png(data_dict, "figures/tbl_data_dictionary.png",
               title = "Variables used in this report", note = dict_note,
               align = c("l", "l", "l", "l"),
               wrap = c(`Plain-language name` = 22, Type = 16, Description = 52))

data_dict |>
  kbl(booktabs = TRUE, caption = "Variables used in this report",
      align = c("l", "l", "l", "l")) |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), font_size = 9) |>
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "2cm", monospace = TRUE) |>
  column_spec(2, width = "3.4cm") |>
  column_spec(3, width = "2.4cm") |>
  column_spec(4, width = "7cm") |>
  footnote(general = dict_note,
           general_title = "Note: ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

# 2. Numerical variables

```{r numeric-table}
# ==============================================================================
# Summary statistics table (replaces describe(c_df))
# ==============================================================================
num_info <- tibble(
  variable    = c("U_short", "f_shimer", "lambda_t"),
  Measure     = c("Short-term unemployed (people)",
                  "Job-finding probability",
                  "Job-finding rate"),
  digits      = c(0, 3, 3)
)

fmt <- function(x, d) ifelse(d == 0, comma(x, accuracy = 1), sprintf("%.3f", x))

num_table <- c_df |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(Mean      = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Median    = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            `Std. dev.` = sd(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Min       = min(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            Max       = max(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  left_join(num_info, by = "variable") |>
  mutate(Mean = fmt(Mean, digits),
         Median = fmt(Median, digits),
         `Std. dev.` = fmt(`Std. dev.`, digits),
         Min = fmt(Min, digits),
         Max = fmt(Max, digits)) |>
  select(Measure, Mean, Median, `Std. dev.`, Min, Max)

num_note <- sprintf("Each statistic is computed across %d months. Std. dev. shows typical month-to-month variation. A large gap between the mean and the median points to a few unusually extreme months.",
                    nrow(c_df))

# Save the table as a figure
save_table_png(num_table, "figures/tbl_numeric_summary.png",
               title = "Summary of monthly labor market measures",
               note = paste("How to read:", num_note),
               align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"))

num_table |>
  kbl(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r", "r", "r", "r"),
      caption = "Summary of monthly labor market measures") |>
  kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position")) |>
  row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
  column_spec(1, width = "5cm") |>
  footnote(general = num_note,
           general_title = "How to read: ", footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
```

```{r numeric-plots-prep}
var_labels <- c(U_short  = "Short-term unemployed (count)",
                f_shimer = "Job-finding probability (Shimer)",
                lambda_t = "Job-finding rate (continuous time)")

c_long <- c_df |>
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "variable", values_to = "value") |>
  mutate(variable = factor(variable, levels = names(var_labels), labels = var_labels))

c_stats <- c_long |>
  group_by(variable) |>
  summarise(mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            median = median(value, na.rm = TRUE),
            .groups = "drop")
```

```{r histograms, fig.width=10, fig.height=4.5, out.width="100%"}
# ---- Histograms with mean and median lines ----
p_hist <- ggplot(c_long, aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(bins = 30, fill = col_main, color = "white", alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = c_stats, aes(xintercept = median, color = "Median"),
             linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(data = c_stats, aes(xintercept = mean, color = "Mean"),
             linewidth = 0.9, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Median = col_accent, Mean = "black"), name = NULL) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.08))) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free", ncol = 3) +
  labs(title = "Distributions of the unemployment flow variables",
       subtitle = "Monthly observations, January 2005 onward",
       x = NULL, y = "Number of months") +
  theme_proj()
print(p_hist)
ggsave("figures/num_histograms.png", p_hist, width = 11, height = 4.5, dpi = 200)
```

```{r boxplots, fig.width=8, fig.height=6.5, out.width="90%"}
# ---- Boxplots ----
p_box <- ggplot(c_long, aes(x = value, y = "")) +
  geom_boxplot(fill = col_main, color = col_main, alpha = 0.3, width = 0.5,
               outlier.color = col_accent, outlier.size = 2.2) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = label_number(scale_cut = cut_short_scale())) +
  facet_wrap(~ variable, scales = "free_x", ncol = 1) +
  labs(title = "Spread and outliers",
       subtitle = "Orange points lie beyond 1.5 x IQR from the box",
       x = NULL, y = NULL) +
  theme_proj() +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
print(p_box)
ggsave("figures/num_boxplots.png", p_box, width = 8, height = 6.5, dpi = 200)
```

# 3. Categorical variables

Each table shows how many person-month records fall into each category and the share of
the total. "Not in universe" means the survey question did not apply to that person.

```{r prop-function}
# ==============================================================================
# Proportion table function (replaces prop_tbl printouts)
# ==============================================================================
prop_kable <- function(data, var, caption, note = NULL, file = NULL) {
  d <- data |>
    count({{ var }}) |>
    filter(!is.na({{ var }})) |>
    arrange(desc(n)) |>
    mutate(share = n / sum(n))

  n_missing <- nrow(data) - sum(d$n)

  out <- d |>
    transmute(
      Category = as.character({{ var }}) |>
        str_replace("^NILF", "Not in labor force") |>
        str_replace("^NIU$", "Not in universe"),
      Observations = comma(n),
      Share = ifelse(share < 0.001, "<0.1%", percent(share, accuracy = 0.1))
    )

  tbl <- bind_rows(out,
                   tibble(Category = "Total",
                          Observations = comma(sum(d$n)),
                          Share = "100.0%"))

  notes <- c(note,
             if (n_missing > 0)
               paste0(comma(n_missing), " records with missing or unlabeled values are excluded.")) 

  # Save the table as a figure
  if (!is.null(file)) {
    save_table_png(tbl, file, title = caption,
                   note = paste(notes, collapse = " "),
                   align = c("l", "r", "r"), bold_last_row = TRUE)
  }

  k <- tbl |>
    kbl(booktabs = TRUE, align = c("l", "r", "r"), caption = caption) |>
    kable_styling(latex_options = c("striped", "hold_position"), full_width = FALSE) |>
    row_spec(0, bold = TRUE) |>
    row_spec(nrow(tbl), bold = TRUE)

  if (length(notes) > 0) {
    k <- k |> footnote(general = notes, general_title = "Note: ",
                       footnote_as_chunk = TRUE)
  }
  k
}
```

## Employment status

```{r empstat-table}
prop_kable(p_df, EMPSTAT, "Employment status of survey respondents",
           note = "Observations are person-month records.",
           file = "figures/tbl_empstat.png")
```

```{r empstat-plot, fig.width=9, fig.height=6, out.width="100%"}
# ---- Bar chart function: horizontal, sorted, with percent labels ----
bar_plot <- function(data, var, title, subtitle = NULL, fill = col_main) {
  d <- data |>
    count({{ var }}) |>
    filter(!is.na({{ var }})) |>
    mutate(prop = n / sum(n),
           category = fct_reorder(as.character({{ var }}), n),
           label = ifelse(prop < 0.001, "<0.1%", percent(prop, accuracy = 0.1)))

  n_missing <- nrow(data) - sum(d$n)
  cap <- paste0("n = ", comma(sum(d$n)), " observations",
                if (n_missing > 0) paste0(" (", comma(n_missing), " with missing/unlabeled values excluded)"))

  ggplot(d, aes(x = prop, y = category)) +
    geom_col(fill = fill, width = 0.72) +
    geom_text(aes(label = label), hjust = -0.12, size = 3.6, color = "grey25") +
    scale_x_continuous(labels = percent, expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.14))) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle, caption = cap,
         x = "Share of observations", y = NULL) +
    theme_proj() +
    theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank())
}

p_emp <- bar_plot(p_df, EMPSTAT, "Employment status",
                  "Share of person-month observations", fill = col_main)
print(p_emp)
ggsave("figures/cat_empstat.png", p_emp, width = 9, height = 6, dpi = 200)
```
